outcome: The top object of the stack resolves each time all players pass in succession.
A triggered ability whose intervening-if condition is false on resolution is removed from the stack and does nothing.
A spell or ability with all targets illegal on resolution does not resolve (a spell goes to its owner's graveyard); with some legal targets it resolves and skips the illegal ones.
Instructions are carried out in written order, with later text modifying earlier text, such as a destroyed creature being unable to regenerate.

note: APNAP choice ordering for multi-player actions

outcome: Actions on multiple players or objects are processed simultaneously where possible, otherwise one at a time in APNAP order.
A spell cast during resolution goes on top of the stack without priority and the resolving object continues to resolve.
Game information is determined once when applied, and a departed object's last known information is used.
An effect looking back in time counts objects that met the criteria at that earlier time, even if they no longer do.
An effect referring to a characteristic checks only that characteristic, so destroying all nonblack creatures spares a white-and-black creature.
An ability still affects an untargeted object it referred to in its cost or trigger even after that object changed characteristics.
An object that can legally resolve and leaves the stack once resolving begins still resolves fully.
A resolved instant or sorcery goes to its owner's graveyard and a resolved ability ceases to exist.
Abilities that trigger on resolution trigger once all resolution steps are completed.
A targetless permanent spell enters the battlefield under its controller's control.
A permanent spell with an illegal target does not resolve and goes to the graveyard, unless it is a bestowed Aura or mutating creature spell, which resolves as a creature spell.
A resolving Aura spell enters the battlefield attached to its target.
A resolving mutating creature spell merges with its target permanent.
A permanent spell that cannot enter the battlefield is put into its owner's graveyard.
A resolving copy of a permanent spell becomes a token that is not treated as created.
A delayed triggered ability from a static ability on the stack is created as the permanent enters the battlefield.
